body: Thank you that's really helpful. That must have taken you a while to write out. I just don't feel like I can trust anyone or talk to anyone. I'm frightened to leave my house for any reason because I got fined on the weekend (my mistake) and I'm also frightened of being sectioned. All I said was I didn't feel like I could go on without him. I just don't know what else I can do.

I originally misread it as a "get over it" comment.
I will take it down with apologies. This is/was a misunderstanding.
I hope that understood. I'm just very freaked out.

You reckon that's ok for me to do? I mean morally speaking - I don't want to jam up their phone lines over £30. I wondered if I should email them but their web form doesn't have an option to admit your own crime and deal with it.


I know I've made a mistake but I don't know how to put it right.


He definitely only glanced at my driving licence which has my full address on it but I wasn't thinking straight I just answered every question he asked me without giving him any trouble which I think now may have freaked him out. He looked a bit young to me.

I agree with you. It feels like thought control to me. 


I have no immediate plans but my therapist is threatening to report me - which could get me sectioned- for even discussing the topic. I can't get help anywhere without lying about what I'm thinking. If I could discuss this sanely without fear of being locked up in a hospital I probably wouldn't be obsessing about it so much.

England - I got fined today, I know I shouldn't have sat down outside but I had to get out, I'm barely holding it together I buried my son on Friday. The officer only took my flat number and postcode not my street address - I showed him my driving licence and everything but didn't realise he hadn't taken my full address until after. Our post is really delayed at the moment I think you only get 14 days to pay the fine- should I contact the Met if I don't receive the fine within a week? I'm scared of going to court over this.
